info.name: Ticket System API
info.description:
Requests and tests for every endpoint of the ticket system Web API.

How to use:
1. Start the API (dotnet run in src/TicketSystem.Api). The default address is http://localhost:5119; change the variable baseUrl if yours differs.
2. Run folder "0. Login" first. It stores the tokens of the seeded accounts (password Password123!).
3. Run the folders 1 to 4 in order, or the whole collection with the Collection Runner. Every request checks the answer.

The WebSocket endpoint /ws/tickets is not part of the collection. Open it in Postman as a new WebSocket request: ws://localhost:5119/ws/tickets?access_token=<token of a support person or the administrator>.

item.name: 0. Login (run this folder first)
item.description: Signs in with the seeded accounts and stores their tokens in collection variables. All other requests use these tokens.

request.description: Signs in as the user Kati Kask and keeps the token in the collection variable tokenKati.

exec: pm.test("Answer has a token and a user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty; pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql("kati.kask@ticketsystem.local"); });

request.description: Signs in as the user Toomas Mets and keeps the token in the collection variable tokenToomas.

exec: pm.test("Answer has a token and a user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty; pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql("toomas.mets@ticketsystem.local"); });

request.description: Signs in as the support person Mari Maasikas and keeps the token in the collection variable tokenMari.

exec: pm.test("Answer has a token and a user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty; pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql("mari.maasikas@ticketsystem.local"); });

request.description: Signs in as the technical account of the Worker Service and keeps the token in the collection variable tokenService.

exec: pm.test("Answer has a token and a user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty; pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql("service@ticketsystem.local"); });

request.description: Creates an account with the role User and returns a token. The email contains a timestamp, so the request can be repeated.

exec: pm.test("New account has the role User", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().user.role).to.eql("User"); });

request.description: Returns the signed-in user.

exec: pm.test("It is Kati Kask", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().displayName).to.eql("Kati Kask"); });

request.description: Public. All ticket categories sorted by name.
Public. Priorities from the lowest to the highest level with the hours to the deadline.

exec: pm.test("Levels go up", function () { const levels = pm.response.json().map(p => p.level); pm.expect(levels).to.eql([...levels].sort((a, b) => a - b)); });

request.description: Support staff and administrator only. The people for the assignee filter. Contains no email addresses.

exec: pm.test("Mari Maasikas is listed and no email is shown", function () { const people = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(people.map(p => p.displayName)).to.include("Mari Maasikas"); pm.expect(people[0]).to.not.have.property("email"); });

item.name: 2. Ticket lifecycle (in order)
item.description: Follows one ticket from creation to resolution. Run the requests in order, or run the whole folder with the Collection Runner.

request.description: A user creates a ticket. The state is New and the deadline comes from the priority.

exec: pm.test("Ticket is New and has a deadline", function () { pm.expect(ticket.status).to.eql("New"); pm.expect(new Date(ticket.deadline).getTime()).to.be.above(new Date(ticket.createdAt).getTime()); });
pm.test("Priority and category are kept", function () { pm.expect(ticket.priority.id).to.eql(2); pm.expect(ticket.category.id).to.eql(1); });
pm.test("It is the created ticket", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("ticketId"))); });

request.description: An ordinary user only sees own tickets. The newest ticket comes first by default.

exec: pm.test("The new ticket is first", function () { pm.expect(page.items[0].id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("ticketId"))); });
pm.test("Page information is present", function () { pm.expect(page).to.include.keys("page", "pageSize", "totalCount", "totalPages"); });
pm.test("Every ticket belongs to Kati", function () { pm.expect(page.items.every(t => t.createdBy.id === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("katiId")))).to.be.true; });

request.description: The author can edit a ticket while it is New. Changing the priority recalculates the deadline.
Support sees all tickets. Filters: state, text search, sorting by the deadline (soonest first) and paging.
Only support can take a ticket, and only when it is New and has no assignee. The state becomes InProgress.

exec: pm.test("InProgress with Mari as assignee", function () { pm.expect(ticket.status).to.eql("InProgress"); pm.expect(ticket.assignee.id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("marId"))); });

request.description: Another support person cannot take a ticket that is already in work.

exec: pm.test("Problem details have a detail", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.be.a("string"); });
pm.test("Every ticket is Mari's", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().items.every(t => t.assignee && t.assignee.id === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("marId")))).to.be.true; });

request.description: Comments come oldest first.

exec: pm.test("Two comments in order", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c[0].author.displayName).to.eql("Kati Kask"); });

request.description: Only the assignee or an administrator can change the state. InProgress to Resolved sets the resolution time.

exec: pm.test("Resolved with a resolution time", function () { const t = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(t.status).to.eql("Resolved"); pm.expect(t.resolvedAt).to.not.be.null; });

request.description: Administrator only. Average time from creation to resolution, in hours, by category and by support person.

exec: pm.test("There is at least one resolved ticket", function () { pm.expect(stats.resolvedCount).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(stats.averageHours).to.be.a("number"); });

request.description: Resolved back to InProgress clears the resolution time.

exec: pm.test("No resolution time", function () { const t = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(t.status).to.eql("InProgress"); pm.expect(t.resolvedAt).to.be.null; });

request.description: Every change is logged with the old and new value and the user.

exec: pm.test("Log has the expected actions", function () { const actions = pm.response.json().map(e => e.action); pm.expect(actions).to.include.members(["Created", "Assigned", "StatusChanged"]); });

request.description: Used by the Worker Service: unresolved tickets whose deadline has passed.

exec: pm.test("Only late tickets", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().every(t => t.status !== "Resolved" && new Date(t.deadline).getTime() < Date.now())).to.be.true; });

item.name: 3. Errors and permissions
item.description: Requests that must be refused. They need the ticket from folder 2.

Create with a too short title

Only the Support role can take tickets.

item.name: Status change by another support person (Jaan)

request.description: New is set by the system. A ticket cannot go back to it.

item.name: Escalate a ticket that is not late (Service)

request.description: Only the service account can escalate, and only when the deadline has passed.
Administrator only. Removes the ticket together with its comments and log.
